   5 /**
   6  * User input library
   7  * Replacement for $_GET and $_POST
   8  * Do not handle $_COOKIES !
   9  *
  10  * @version     1.11 $Revision: 14130 $
  11  * @copyright   (c) 2001-2012, Universite catholique de Louvain (UCL)
  12  * @author      Claroline Team <info@claroline.net>
  13  * @author      Frederic Minne <zefredz@claroline.net>
  14  * @license     http://www.gnu.org/copyleft/gpl.html
  15  *              GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE version 2 or later
  16  * @package     utils
  17  */
  18  
  19 FromKernel::uses ( 'utils/validator.lib' );
  20 
  21 /**
  22  * Data Input Exception, thrown when an input value does not match
  23  * a filter or is missing
  24  */
  25 class Claro_Input_Exception extends Exception{};
  26 
  27 /**
  28  * Defines the required methods for a data input object
  29  */
  30 interface Claro_Input
  31 {
  32     /**
  33      * Get a value given its name.
  34      * @param   string $name variable name
  35      * @param   mixed $default default value (if $name is missing in the input)
  36      * @return  mixed value of $name in input data or $default value
  37      * @throws  Claro_Input_Exception on failure
  38      */
  39     public function get( $name, $default = null );
  40     /**
  41      * Get a value given its name, the value must be set in the data
  42      * but can be empty
  43      * @param   string $name variable name
  44      * @return  mixed value of $name
  45      * @throws  Claro_Input_Exception on failure or if $name is missing
  46      */
  47     public function getMandatory( $name );
  48 }
  49 
  50 /**
  51  * Array based data input class
  52  */
  53 class Claro_Input_Array implements Claro_Input
  54 {
  55     protected $input;
  56     protected $_notSet;
  57     
  58     /**
  59      * @param   array $input
  60      */
  61     public function __construct( $input )
  62     {
  63         $this->input = $input;
  64         // create a singleton object for the getMandatory method
  65         // this object will be used to check if a value is defined
  66         // in the input data in order to avoid pitfalls with the empty()
  67         // PHP function
  68         $this->_notSet = (object) null;
  69     }
  70     
  71     /**
  72      * Is considered empty : string(0), null, array(0), empty stdClass object
  73      * @param mixed $value
  74      * @return bool 
  75      */
  76     protected static function isEmpty( $value )
  77     {
  78         return !( is_numeric ( $value ) || is_bool ( $value ) || ( is_object ( $value ) && get_class($value) != 'stdClass' ) ) 
  79                 && empty( $value );
  80     }
  81     
  82     /**
  83      * @see     Claro_Input
  84      */
  85     public function get( $name, $default = null )
  86     {
  87         // the variable exists
  88         if ( array_key_exists( $name, $this->input ) )
  89         {
  90             $value = $this->input[$name];
  91             
  92             // the variable is considered empty but a default value is given
  93             if ( !is_null( $default ) 
  94                 && self::isEmpty ( $value )  )
  95             {
  96                 return $default;
  97             }
  98             // no default value given
  99             else
 100             {
 101                 return $value;
 102             }
 103         }
 104         else
 105         {
 106             return $default;
 107         }
 108     }
 109     
 110     /**
 111      * @see     Claro_Input
 112      */
 113     public function getMandatory( $name )
 114     {
 115         // get the value of the requested variable and give the _notSet
 116         // singleton object as the default value so we can check if the
 117         // varaible was set without having issues with the empty() function
 118         $ret = $this->get( $name, $this->_notSet );
 119         
 120         // check if $ret is the instance of the _notSet singleton object
 121         // if it is the case, the requested variable has not been set
 122         // in the input data so we have to throw an exception
 123         if ( $ret === $this->_notSet )
 124         {
 125             throw new Claro_Input_Exception(
 126                 "{$name} not found in ".get_class($this)." !" );
 127         }
 128         else
 129         {
 130             return $ret;
 131         }
 132     }
 133 }
 134 
 135 /**
 136  * Data input class with filters callback for validation
 137  */
 138 class Claro_Input_Validator implements Claro_Input
 139 {
 140     protected $validators;
 141     protected $validatorsForAll;
 142     protected $input;
 143     
 144     /**
 145      * @param   Claro_Input $input
 146      */
 147     public function __construct( Claro_Input $input )
 148     {
 149         $this->validators = array();
 150         $this->validatorsForAll = array();
 151         $this->input = $input;
 152     }
 153     
 154     /**
 155      * Set a validator for the given variable
 156      * @param   string $name variable name
 157      * @param   Claro_Validator $validator validator object
 158      * @throws  Claro_Input_Exception if the filter callback is not callable
 159      */
 160     public function setValidator( $name, Claro_Validator $validator )
 161     {
 162         if ( ! array_key_exists( $name, $this->validators ) )
 163         {
 164             $this->validators[$name] = array();
 165         }
 166         
 167         $validatorCallback = array( $validator, 'isValid' );
 168         
 169         if ( ! is_callable( $validatorCallback ) )
 170         {
 171             throw new Claro_Input_Exception ("Invalid validator callback : " 
 172                 . $this->getFilterCallbackString($validatorCallback));
 173         }
 174         
 175         $this->validators[$name][] = $validatorCallback;
 176     }
 177     
 178     /**
 179      * Set a validator for all variables
 180      * @param   string $name variable name
 181      * @param   Claro_Validator $validator validator object
 182      * @throws  Claro_Input_Exception if the filter callback is not callable
 183      */
 184     public function setValidatorForAll( Claro_Validator $validator )
 185     {
 186         $validatorCallback = array( $validator, 'isValid' );
 187         
 188         if ( ! is_callable( $validatorCallback ) )
 189         {
 190             throw new Claro_Input_Exception ("Invalid validator callback : " 
 191                 . $this->getFilterCallbackString($validatorCallback));
 192         }
 193         
 194         $this->validatorsForAll[] = $validatorCallback;
 195     }
 196     
 197     /**
 198      * @see     Claro_Input
 199      * @throws  Claro_Input_Exception if $value does not pass the validator
 200      */
 201     public function get( $name, $default = null )
 202     {
 203         $tainted = $this->input->get( $name, $default );
 204         
 205         // we need to detect that the default value has been returned to avoid 
 206         // running it to the validator
 207         if ( ( is_null( $default ) && is_null( $tainted ) )
 208             || $tainted == $default )
 209         {
 210             return $default;
 211         }
 212         else
 213         {
 214             return $this->validate( $name, $tainted );
 215         }
 216     }
 217     
 218     /**
 219      * @see     Claro_Input
 220      * @throws  Claro_Input_Exception if $value does not pass the validator
 221      */
 222     public function getMandatory( $name )
 223     {
 224         $tainted = $this->input->getMandatory( $name );
 225         
 226         return $this->validate( $name, $tainted );
 227     }
 228     
 229     /**
 230      * @param   string $name
 231      * @param   mixed $tainted value
 232      * @throws  Claro_Validator_Exception if $value does not pass the
 233      * filter for $name
 234      */
 235     public function validate( $name, $tainted )
 236     {
 237         // validators for all variables if any
 238         if ( !empty ($this->validatorsForAll ) )
 239         {
 240             foreach ( $this->validatorsForAll as $validatorForAllCallback )
 241             {
 242                 if ( ! call_user_func( $validatorForAllCallback, $tainted ) )
 243                 {
 244                     throw new Claro_Validator_Exception(
 245                         get_class( $validatorForAllCallback[0] )
 246                         . " : {$name} does not pass the validator !" );
 247                 }
 248             }
 249         }
 250         
 251         // validators for the requested variable
 252         if ( array_key_exists( $name, $this->validators ) )
 253         {
 254             foreach ( $this->validators[$name] as $validatorCallback )
 255             {
 256                 if ( ! call_user_func( $validatorCallback, $tainted ) )
 257                 {
 258                     throw new Claro_Validator_Exception(
 259                         get_class( $validatorCallback[0] )
 260                         . " : {$name} does not pass the validator !" );
 261                 }
 262             }
 263         }
 264         
 265         return $tainted;
 266     }
 267 }
 268 
 269 /**
 270  * User input class to replace $_REQUEST
 271  * @since Claroline 1.11, Claro_Validator_CustomNotEmpty is no more ssigned to 
 272  *  all variables because it causes the system to refuse to return the default 
 273  *  value for an empty string
 274  */
 275 class Claro_UserInput
 276 {        
 277     protected static $instance = false;
 278     
 279     /**
 280      * Get user input object
 281      * @return  Claro_Input_Validator
 282      */
 283     public static function getInstance()
 284     {
 285         if ( ! self::$instance )
 286         {
 287             // Create an input validator instance using the $_GET
 288             // and $_POST super arrays
 289             self::$instance = new Claro_Input_Validator( 
 290                 new Claro_Input_Array( array_merge( $_GET, $_POST ) ) );
 291         }
 292         
 293         return self::$instance;
 294     }
 295 }

  17 
  18 interface CountableIterator extends Countable, Iterator{};
  19 
  20 interface CountableSeekableIterator extends CountableIterator, SeekableIterator{};
  21 
  22 
  23 /**
  24  * Define a generic array row to object array iterator
  25  * You must extends it and implement the current() method
  26  */
  27 abstract class RowToObjectArrayIterator implements CountableIterator
  28 {
  29 
  30   protected $collection = null;
  31   protected $currentIndex = 0;
  32   protected $maxIndex;
  33   protected $keys = null;
  34   
  35   /**
  36    *
  37    * @param Array $array 
  38    */
  39   public function __construct($array) 
  40   {
  41 
  42     $this->collection = $array;
  43     $this->maxIndex = count( $array );
  44     $this->keys = array_keys( $array );
  45   }
  46 
  47   public function key()
  48   {
  49     return $this->keys[$this->currentIndex];
  50   }
  51 
  52   public function next()
  53   {
  54     ++$this->currentIndex;
  55   }
  56 
  57   public function rewind()
  58   {
  59     $this->currentIndex = 0;
  60   }
  61 
  62   public function valid()
  63   {
  64     return ( isset($this->keys[$this->currentIndex]) );
  65   }
  66   
  67   public function count()
  68   {
  69       return count($this->collection);
  70   }
  71   
  72 }
  73 
  74 /**
  75  * Define a generic row to object iterator iterator
  76  * You must extends it and implement the current() method
  77  */
  78 abstract class RowToObjectIteratorIterator implements CountableIterator
  79 {
  80     protected $internalIterator;
  81     
  82     /**
  83      * Constructor
  84      * @param CountableIterator $internalIterator
  85      */
  86     public function __construct(CountableIterator $internalIterator)
  87     {
  88         $this->internalIterator = $internalIterator;
  89     }
  90     
  91     public function next ()
  92     {
  93         return $this->internalIterator->next();
  94     }
  95     
  96     public function key ()
  97     {
  98         return $this->internalIterator->key();
  99     }
 100     
 101     public function valid ()
 102     {
 103         return $this->internalIterator->valid();
 104     }
 105     
 106     public function rewind ()
 107     {
 108         return $this->internalIterator->rewind();
 109     }
 110     
 111     public function count ()
 112     {
 113         return count( $this->internalIterator );
 114     }
 115 }

   3 // vim: expandtab sw=4 ts=4 sts=4:
   4 
   5 /**
   6  * Data validator library
   7  *
   8  * @version     1.11 $Revision: 14130 $
   9  * @copyright   (c) 2001-2012, Universite catholique de Louvain (UCL)
  10  * @author      Claroline Team <info@claroline.net>
  11  * @author      Frederic Minne <zefredz@claroline.net>
  12  * @license     http://www.gnu.org/copyleft/gpl.html
  13  *              GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE version 2 or later
  14  * @package     utils
  15  */
  16 
  17 interface Claro_Validator
  18 {
  19     /**
  20      * Check if the given value is valid
  21      * @param   mixed $value
  22      * @return  boolean
  23      */
  24     public function isValid( $value );
  25 }
  26 
  27 /**
  28  * Exception class for the Validator library
  29  */
  30 class Claro_Validator_Exception extends Exception{};
  31 
  32 /**
  33  * Validator that uses a given PHP callback to validate a value
  34  */
  35 class Claro_Validator_Callback implements Claro_Validator
  36 {
  37     protected $callback;
  38     
  39     /**
  40      * @param   callback $callback;
  41      * @throws  Claro_Validator_Exception if $callback is not callable
  42      */
  43     public function __construct( $callback )
  44     {
  45         if ( ! is_callable( $this->callback ) )
  46         {
  47             throw new Claro_Validator_Exception("Callback ".var_export($this->callback, true)."is not callable");
  48         }
  49         else
  50         {
  51             $this->callback = $callback;
  52         }
  53     }
  54     
  55     /**
  56      * @see Claro_Validator
  57      */
  58     public function isValid( $value )
  59     {
  60         return call_user_func( $this->callback, $value );
  61     }
  62 }
  63 
  64 /**
  65  * Validator that checks the data type of a value
  66  */
  67 class Claro_Validator_ValueType implements Claro_Validator
  68 {
  69     protected static $supportedType = array(
  70         'alnum'     => 'ctype_alnum',
  71         'alpha'     => 'ctype_alpha',
  72         'array'     => 'is_array',
  73         'bool'      => 'is_bool',
  74         'boolstr'   => array('Claro_Validator_ValueType', 'booleanString'),
  75         'digit'     => 'ctype_digit',
  76         'float'     => 'is_float',
  77         'floatstr'  => array('Claro_Validator_ValueType', 'floatString'),
  78         'int'       => 'is_int',
  79         'intstr'    => array('Claro_Validator_ValueType', 'integerString'),
  80         'lower'     => 'ctype_lower',
  81         'null'      => 'is_null',
  82         'numeric'   => 'is_numeric',
  83         'object'    => 'is_object',
  84         'space'     => 'ctype_space',
  85         'string'    => 'is_string',
  86         'upper'     => 'ctype_upper',
  87         'xdigit'    => 'ctype_xdigit',
  88         );
  89     
  90     /**
  91      * Allowed types are
  92      *  - alnum     : the value is an alpha-numeric string
  93      *  - alpha     : the value only containes alphabetical chars
  94      *  - array     : the value is an array
  95      *  - bool      : the value is a boolean
  96      *  - boolstr   : the value is the string 'true' or 'false'
  97      *  - digit     : the value is a string containing only digits
  98      *  - float     : the value is a float
  99      *  - floatstr  : the value is a float or the string representation of a float
 100      *  - int       : the value is an integer
 101      *  - intstr    : the value is a integer or the string representation of an integer
 102      *  - lower     : ths value is a lower case string
 103      *  - null      : the value is null
 104      *  - numeric   : the value is a number or a string representation of a number
 105      *  - object    : the value is an object
 106      *  - space     : the value is a string only containing white spaces
 107      *  - string    : the value is a string
 108      *  - upper     : the value is an upper case
 109      *  - xdigit    : the value is a string representation of an hexadecimal number
 110      * WARNING : do not use int, float, bool for strings representations, it will
 111      * fail. Use digit, numeric, intstr, floatstr and boolstr instead.
 112      * @param   string $type;
 113      * @throws  Claro_Validator_Exception if $type is not supported
 114      */    
 115     public function __construct( $type )
 116     {
 117         if ( array_key_exists( $type, self::$supportedType ) )
 118         {
 119             $this->type = $type;
 120         }
 121         else
 122         {
 123             throw new Claro_Validator_Exception("Unsupported type {$type}");
 124         }
 125     }
 126     
 127     /**
 128      * @see     Claro_Validator
 129      */
 130     public function isValid( $value )
 131     {
 132         if ( call_user_func( self::$supportedType[$this->type], $value ) )
 133         {
 134             return true;
 135         }
 136         else
 137         {
 138             return false;
 139         }
 140     }
 141     
 142     private static function booleanString( $value )
 143     {
 144         return strtolower( $value ) == 'true' || strtolower( $value ) == 'false';
 145     }
 146     
 147     private static function floatString( $value )
 148     {
 149         return is_numeric( $value ) && (float) $value == $value;
 150     }
 151     
 152     private static function integerString( $value )
 153     {
 154         return is_numeric( $value ) && (int) $value == $value;
 155     }
 156 }
 157 
 158 /**
 159  * Validator that checks if the value is in a given list
 160  */
 161 class Claro_Validator_AllowedList implements Claro_Validator
 162 {
 163     protected $allowedValues;
 164     
 165     /**
 166      * @param   array $allowedValues
 167      */
 168     public function __construct( $allowedValues )
 169     {
 170         $this->allowedValues = $allowedValues;
 171     }
 172     
 173     /**
 174      * @see     Claro_Validator
 175      */
 176     public function isValid( $value )
 177     {
 178         return in_array( $value, $this->allowedValues );
 179     }
 180 }
 181 
 182 /**
 183  * Validator that uses a PCRE regular expression to check a value
 184  */
 185 class Claro_Validator_Pcre implements Claro_Validator
 186 {
 187     protected $regexp;
 188     
 189     /**
 190      * @param   string $regexp PCRE regular expression
 191      */
 192     public function __construct( $regexp )
 193     {
 194         $this->regexp = $regexp;
 195     }
 196     
 197     /**
 198      * @see     Claro_Validator
 199      */
 200     public function isValid( $value )
 201     {
 202         return preg_match( $this->regexp, $value );
 203     }
 204 }
 205 
 206 /**
 207  * Validator that checks if a value has the given file extension
 208  */
 209 class Claro_Validator_FileExtension implements Claro_Validator
 210 {
 211     protected $extension;
 212     
 213     /**
 214      * @param   string $extension file extension
 215      */
 216     public function __construct( $extension )
 217     {
 218         $extension = $extension[0] == '.'
 219             ? substr( $extension, 1 )
 220             : $extension
 221             ;
 222             
 223         $this->extension = $extension;
 224     }
 225     
 226     /**
 227      * @see     Claro_Validator
 228      */
 229     public function isValid( $value )
 230     {
 231         return ( pathinfo( $value, PATHINFO_EXTENSION ) == $this->extension );
 232     }
 233 }
 234 
 235 /**
 236  * Validator that checks if a value is not empty based on PHP's empty()
 237  */
 238 class Claro_Validator_NotEmpty implements Claro_Validator
 239 {
 240     /**
 241      * @see     Claro_Validator
 242      */
 243     public function isValid( $value )
 244     {
 245         return ( !empty( $value ) );
 246     }
 247 }
 248 
 249 /**
 250  * Validator that checks if a value is not null based on PHP's is_null()
 251  */
 252 class Claro_Validator_NotNull implements Claro_Validator
 253 {
 254     /**
 255      * @see     Claro_Validator
 256      */
 257     public function isValid( $value )
 258     {
 259         return ( !is_null( $value ) );
 260     }
 261 }
 262 
 263 /**
 264  * Validator that checks if a value is not empty but considers
 265  * '0', 0 and false as not empty !
 266  */
 267 class Claro_Validator_CustomNotEmpty implements Claro_Validator
 268 {
 269     /**
 270      * @see     Claro_Validator
 271      */
 272     public function isValid( $value )
 273     {
 274         return ( is_numeric($value) || is_bool($value) || !empty( $value ) );
 275     }
 276 }

 279 
 280 class Claro_Validator_AlwaysFail implements Claro_Validator
 281 {
 282     /**
 283      * @see     Claro_Validator
 284      */
 285     public function isValid( $value )
 286     {
 287         return false;
 288     }
 289 }
 290 
 291 class Claro_Validator_AlwaysSucceed implements Claro_Validator
 292 {
 293     /**
 294      * @see     Claro_Validator
 295      */
 296     public function isValid( $value )
 297     {
 298         return true;
 299     }

2050 $_lang['blockAssignmentsHelp'] = '<p>
2051 Assignment tool is a publication area for students. The course manager creates one or several assignment ( different zones of publication ) where the students will be able to publish their work.<br /><br />
2052 Each assignment can have different objectives or requirements : publication must be a file, or a text or a text and a file, publication can be made for a groupe instead of for a single user,...<br /><br />
2053 Students have the ability to modify their work after submission and the course manager can give them a feedback about their submissions.
2054 </p>
2055 <hr />
2056 <h4>Create an assignment</h4>
2057 <p>To create a new assignment course manager must enter in the assignment tool and click on the link "Create a new assignment".
2058 </p>
2059 <p>The form that is shown ask the course manager for&nbsp;:
2060 </p>
2061 <ul><li> a title&nbsp;: the name of the assignment
2062 </li><li> a description&nbsp;: the statement of the assignment, what learners have to do
2063 </li><li> a submission type&nbsp;:
2064 <ul><li> File&nbsp;: any type of file that can be uploaded, keep in mind that there is a size limit that depends on the platform, a text can be joined to describe the file
2065 </li><li> Text only&nbsp;: a text formatted using the wysiwyg editor
2066 </li><li> Text with an attached file&nbsp;: a text formatted using the wysiwyg editor and a file (file is not required)
2067 </li></ul>
2068 </li><li> a start date&nbsp;: date from when the users will be able to post a publication in the assignment
2069 </li><li> a end date&nbsp;: date until when the users will be able to post a publication in the assignment
2070 </li><li> the default publications visibility&nbsp;: choose if the publications will be available or not to others users
2071 </li><li> the assignment type&nbsp;:
2072 <ul><li> individual mode&nbsp;: any authenticated user can post a publication
2073 </li><li> group mode&nbsp;: the user must be a member of at least one group of the course to publish a work and the work will be posted in the name of the group
2074 </li></ul>
2075 </li><li> permission to upload after end date
2076 </li></ul>
2077 <p><br />
2078 <strong>Add an automatic feedback</strong>
2079 </p>
2080 <p>A feedback is a correct version of the assignment.  To add an automatic feedback to an assignment enter the assignment and click on the "Edit automatic feedback" link.  </p>
2081 <p>It can be a text or a file or both a text and a file.  The course manager can choose when this automatic feedback will be shown to users ( after assignment end date or after the first submission of the user in this assignment )
2082 </p>
2083 <hr />
2084 <h4>Works</h4>
2085 <p>Works are the publications uploaded by users.</p>
2086 <p>For each assignment the tool shows a list of all users registered in the course and for each user the title of the first work he published, the number of submissions and the number of feedbacks.
2087 The list of publications related to the user and the assignment can be view by clicking on the name of the user.</p>
2088 <p><strong>Submit a work</strong></p>
2089 <p>If the users has the right to submit a work he will be displayed a link to a submit form.</p>
2090 <p><strong>Work list</strong></p>
2091 <p>As a course manager you have the right to edit, delete, make visible/invisible any of the works.  You can also add a feedback for each work.
2092 </p>
2093 <ul>
2094 <li> <strong>Modify</strong>&nbsp;: If this icon appears it means that user can modify the content of the work, it appears when user is the course manager, when user is looking at his works or at his group works.
2095 </li>
2096 <li> <strong>Delete</strong>&nbsp;: This command allow the course manager to delete a work.
2097 </li>
2098 <li> <strong>Visible</strong>&nbsp;: If this icon appears for a work, it means that the work is visible to the learners. This is just like in the document tool of Claroline. You can change this setting by clicking on the icon.
2099 </li>
2100 <li> <strong>Invisible</strong>&nbsp;: If this icon appears for a work, it means that the work is invisible to the learners. This is just like in the document tool of Claroline. You can change this setting by clicking on the icon.
2101 </li>
2102 <li> <strong>Add feedback</strong>&nbsp;: allows the course manager to publish a feedback about the work of the user.  A feedback can be a file or a text or both with a private comment that only course manager(s) will be able to see and a score in pourcent.
2103 </li>
2104 </ul>
2105 ';
2106 $_lang['blockClaroMainHelp'] = 'Here, lecturers and assistants create and administer
2107  courses websites. Students read (documents, agenda, information) and,
2108  sometimes, do exercises, publish papers, participate in
2109  forum discussions...</p><b>Registration</b><p>The following instructions
2110  only apply if your version of claroline allows self-registration (some sites
2111  register you automatically). <br />If you are a Student, you
2112  just need to register selecting \'Follow courses (student)\', then choose
2113  the courses you would like to follow.</p><p>If you are a Lecturer or an
2114  Assistant, register too, but select \'Create courses (lecturer)\'. You will
2115  then have to fill a form with Course Code, Faculty and Course Title. Once
2116  this is validated, you will be directed to the site you have just created and
2117  allowed to modify its content and organisation according to your
2118  requirements. </p><p>The \'To do\' option is to allow feedback to your claroline website administrators.
2119  Things that you might post here include faults or suggestions for improvements. The \'To do\'
2120  list is linked to on the Home Page of the campus (once
2121  logged in).</p>
2122 <p>The support forum is different. It connects all Claroline users worldwide.
2123 If you don\'t find the answer to a question inside your claroline campus and environment,
2124 post a message there.</p>
2125 <p>The link to Registration (if present) is on the Home Page of the campus
2126  (top right).</p><b>Login</b><p>On your next visit, type login/password
2127  and Ok to access your courses. The URL of the site is';

2196 $_lang['blockDocumentsHelp'] = '<p>The Documents tool is similar to the File Manager of
2197  your desktop computer.</p><p>You can upload files of any type (HTML, Word,
2198  Powerpoint, Excel, Acrobat, Flash, Quicktime, etc.). Your only concern
2199  must be that your students have the corresponding software to read them.
2200  Some file types can contain viruses, it is your responsibilty not to
2201  upload virus contaminated files. It is a worthwhile precaution to check
2202  documents with antivirus software before uploading them.</p>
2203 <hr />
2204 <h4>View modes</h4>
2205 The Claroline document has 2 view mode
2206 <ul>
2207 <li>File list (default)</li>
2208 <li>Thumbnail</li>
2209 </ul>
2210 You can switch between \'file list\' and \'thumbnail\' mode simply by clicking on
2211 the \'File list | Thumbnails\' commands  on the right in the directory toolbar.
2212 <h4>The image viewer</h4>
2213 <ul>
2214 <li>Open the Image Viewer simply by clicking on the name of an image file in the File List mode
2215 or on an image thumbnails in the Thumbnails Mode</li>
2216 <li>Go to next or previous image y clicking on its name or its thumbnails
2217 in the Image Viewer toolbar</li>
2218 <li>Close the Image Viewer simply by clicking either on \'Thumbnails\' or on \'File List\' on the right
2219 in the directory toolbar</li>
2220 </ul>
2221 <h4>Search a ressource</h4>
2222 <ul>
2223 <li>
2224 Click on the \'Search command\' in the upper side of your browser windows.
2225 </li>
2226 <li>
2227 Enter your search patter. You can use \'*\' and \'?\' wildcards for complex research.
2228 </li>
2229 <li>
2230 Click on the \'OK\' button.
2231 </li>
2232 <li>
2233 The search result wil be displayed just beside the directory toolbar.
2234 </li>
2235 </ul>
2236 <hr />
2237 <h4>Managing documents</h4>
2238 This tool has a collection of commands allowing you to upload, edit and
2239 organize your file ressources.
2240 </hr />
2241 <h4>Upload a document</h4>
2242 <ul>
2243 <li>
2244 Click on the \'Upload file\' command in the upper left.
2245 </li>
2246 <li>
2247 Select the file on your computer using the \'Browse\' button in the dialog box.
2248 </li>
2249 <li>
2250 Optionnaly, you can attach a comment to this document. It will be displayed
2251 just below the document line.
2252 <blockquote><small>
2253 <i>Note</i> If you upload a file collection gathered in archive file in <i>ZIP</i> format,
2254 check the \'uncompress zipped (.zip) file on the server\' option to extract them
2255 automatically once the archive is uploaded in your course repositoy on the server.
2256 </small></blockquote>
2257 </li>
2258 <li>
2259 Launch the upload by clicking on the \'Upload\' button.
2260 </li>
2261 </ul>
2262 <h4>Create an hyperlink</h4>
2263 <ul>
2264 <li>
2265 Click on the \'create hyperlink\' command  in the upper side of your browser windows.
2266 </li>
2267 <li>
2268 Fill the \'Name\' field with a specific name to this hyperlink;
2269 </li>
2270 <li>
2271 Type the complete URL of the hyperlink
2272 (example : http://my.domain/my/file.htm).
2273 </li>
2274 <li>
2275 Optionnaly, you can attach a comment to this hyperlink.
2276 It will be displayed just below the hyperlink line.
2277 </li>
2278 </li>
2279 <li>
2280 Validate by clicking on the \'OK\' button.
2281 </li>
2282 </ul>
2283 <h4>Create an HTML document on line</h4>
2284 <ul>
2285 <li> Click on the \'Create document\' command in the upper side of your browser windows.
2286 </li>
2287 <li>
2288 Fill appearing \'Document name\' field with a a name for this document.
2289 </li>
2290 <li>
2291 Enter the document content in the \'Document content\' area.
2292 </li>
2293 <li>
2294 Click on the \'OK\' button once finished.
2295 </li>
2296 </ul>
2297 <p>
2298 This command can be used for writing short documents. To write
2299 longer texts we recommend you to use a more suitable tool on your personal
2300 computer.
2301 </p>
2302 <h4>Rename a document, a directory or a hyperlink</h4>
2303 <ul>
2304 <li>Click on the icon in the \'Edit\' column.
2305 </li>
2306 <li>
2307 Type the new name in the field in the upper side of your browser window.
2308 </li>
2309 <li>
2310 Optionally, you can also add or modify a comment attached to this document.
2311 It will be displayed just below the document line.
2312 </li>
2313 <li>
2314 Validate by clicking on the \'OK\' button.
2315 </li>
2316 </ul>
2317 <p>
2318 <b>Tip. </b>
2319 Documents are presented in alphabetical order. If you want to present them in a
2320 different order, number them: 01, 02, 03...
2321 </p>
2322 <h4>Delete a document, a directory or a hyperlink</h4>
2323 <ul>
2324 <li>
2325 Click on the icon beside the document in the \'Delete\' column.</li>
2326 </ul>
2327 <h4>
2328 Make a document, a directory or a hyperlink invisible to students
2329 </h4>
2330 <ul>
2331 <li>
2332 Click on the icon beside the document in the \'Visible/invisible\' column.
2333 </li>
2334 <li>
2335 The element still exists but it is not visible by students anymore.
2336 </li>
2337 <li>
2338 To make it invisible back again, click once more on the icon beside the document
2339 in the \'Visible/invisible\' column.
2340 </li>
2341 </ul>
2342 <h4>
2343 Add or modify a comment to a document, a directory or a hyperlink
2344 </h4>
2345 <ul>
2346 <li>
2347 Click on the icon beside the document in the \'edit\' column.
2348 </li>
2349 <li>
2350 Type new comment in the corresponding field.
2351 </li>
2352 <li>
2353 Validate by clicking on the \'OK\' button.
2354 </li>
2355 </ul>
2356 <p>
2357 To delete a comment, click on the icon beside the document in the \'Edit\' column,
2358 delete the old comment in the field and click on the \'OK\' button.
2359 <h4>Create a directory</h4>
2360 <ul>
2361 <li>Click on the \'Create directory\' command in the upper side of your browser window.
2362 </li>
2363 <li>
2364 Type the name of your new directory in the corresponding field (top left).
2365 </li>
2366 <li>
2367 Validate by clicking on the \'OK\' button.
2368 </li>
2369 </ul>
2370 <h4>
2371 Move a document a directory or a hyperlink
2372 </h4>
2373 <ul>
2374 <li>
2375 Click on on the icon beside the concernent element in the \'Move\' column.
2376 </li>
2377 <li>
2378 Choose the directory into which you want to move the element in
2379 the corresponding scrolling menu (top left)
2380 <br />Note: the word \'root\' means you cannot go higher than that level in the
2381 document tree of the server).
2382 </li>
2383 <li>
2384 Validate by clicking on the \'OK\' button.
2385 </li>
2386 </ul>
2387 <center>
2388 <p>';
2389 $_lang['blockExercisesHelp'] = '<h4>What is the exercise tool ?</h4>
2390 This tool allow you to create online exercises composed of a list of questions. The questions can be of different kinds, students can fill in the exercises and if they are registered to your course, their scores will be stored and visible in the statitiscs of the course.
2391 <hr />
2392 <h4>Administering the exercises</h4>
2393 <p>To create an Exercise</p>
2394 <ul>
2395 <li> Click on "New exercise", in the start page of the tool (be sure that you are loggued in as teacher of the course or admin)</li>
2396 <li> Enter a name for the exercise in the box</li>
2397 <li> Enter a description</li>
2398 <li> Choose if the user will see all the questions on a single page or one page for each question</li>
2399 <li> I you want to you can also modify the advanced settings (not required)
2400 <ul>
2401 <li> choose a start date</li>
2402 <li> choose a end date</li>
2403 <li> define a time limit</li>
2404 <li> choose the number of allowed attempts</li>
2405 <li> choose if anonymous attempts are allowed (if not allowed there will be no tracking)</li>
2406 <li> choose when the feedback has to be shown</li>
2407 </ul>
2408 </li>
2409 <li> Click on Ok</li>
2410 </ul>
2411 <p>You can now fill your new exercises with new questions or questions from the pool.</p>
2412 <hr />
2413 <h4>Questions</h4>
2414 <h4>Multiple choice questions</h4>
2415 <p>There are two kind of multiple choice question&nbsp;:
2416 </p>
2417 <ul>
2418 <li> Question with unique answer</li>
2419 <li> Question with multiple answer</li>
2420 </ul>
2421 <p>In both case, when you start creating a new question, there are only two possible answers displayed. If you wish to have more possible answers then</p>
2422 <ul>
2423 <li> Press +Answ for each additional answer you require</li>
2424 </ul>
2425 <p>If you wish the reduce the amount of possible answers then </p>
2426 <ul>
2427 <li> Press -Answ for each answer to be removed</li>
2428 </ul>
2429 <p>Then for each answer&nbsp;:</p>
2430 <ul>
2431 <li> Place a tick in the checkbox for the correct answer(s).</li>
2432 <li> In the answer column Enter the text for the possible answers to the questions</li>
2433 <li> In the comment column Enter feedback that is given if a student selects that answer.</li>
2434 <li> Adjust the weighting value. The principle of this scoring table is to define proper weight to number of good answers by question. For instance, if you have a question with 4 answers (possibly more than one right) and the student has two wrong and two right, you can give him half of the points, but you can also decide that this is not satisfactory and give, for instance, maximum points (20) if everything is right and zero points in any other combination.
2435 </li>
2436 </ul>
2437 <h4>Matching question</h4>
2438 <p>In this type of question, the student will have to find the correspondance between the elements of to distinct list.</p>
2439 <p>When you start creating a new question of that kind, there are only two elements in the two list displayed. If you wish to have more possible elements to correspond then</p>
2440 <ul>
2441 <li> Press +elem for each additional answer you require</li>
2442 </ul>
2443 <p>If you wish the reduce the amount of elements then </p>
2444 <ul>
2445 <li> Press -elem for each answer to be removed</li>
2446 </ul>
2447 <p>You can also define the weighting of each answer, they can not be negative. Don\'t forget to click on "ok" to validate your new question.</p>
2448 <h4>\'Fill in blanks\' question</h4>
2449 <p>This type of question is a text with some words missing that the student must fill in.
2450 When you create such a question&nbsp;:
2451 </p>
2452 <ul>
2453 <li> Introduce first the text for the question.</li>
2454 <li> Use brackets [...] to define one or more blanks in the text, put the correct answers between the brackets.
2455 <ul>
2456 <li> <em>example:</em> [British people] live in [United Kingdom].</li>
2457 </ul>
2458 </li>
2459 <li> Click on "next" when done</li>
2460 <li> Define the ponderation for each answer</li>
2461 <li> Click on "Ok" to validate your new question</li>
2462 </ul>
2463 <hr />
2464 <h4>The Pool of questions</h4>
2465 <p>The pool of questions keeps a list of all questions created in the course.  The lists regroups already used question (in one or several exercises) and orphaned question (that are not used in any exercise).</p>
2466 <p>When you delete an exercise, questions of its own are not removed from the database, and can be reused in a new exercise, via the question pool.</p>
2467 <p>The question pool also allows you to reuse the same questions in several exercises.</p>
2468 <p>By default, all questions of your course are shown. You can show the questions related to an exercise, by chosing this one in the drop-down menu "Filter".</p>
2469 <hr />
2470 <h4>How to see my previous scores ?</h4>
2471 <p>Every user can see its own scores below the list of exercises.  As a course manager you can click on the tracking link available for any exercise in the exercises list to have access to the detailled scores of each student of the course.</p>';
2472 $_lang['blockFeedbackHelp'] = 'Feedback is optionnal. It is the correct version of the assignment. If not empty it will be shown to users according to the \'submit feedback\' configuration.';
2473 $_lang['blockForumsHelp'] = 'The forum is a written and asynchronous discussion tool.
2474  Whereas email allows one-to-one dialogue, forums allow public or semi-public
2475  dialogue.</p><p>Technically speaking, the students need only their
2476  browser to use claroline forums.</P><p>To organise forums, click on
2477  \'Administer\'. Discussions are organised in sets and subsets as
2478  following:</p><p><b>Category > Forum > Topic > Answers</b></p>To structure
2479  your students\' discussions, it is necessary to organise catgories and
2480  forums beforehand, leaving the creation of topics and answers to them. By
2481  default, the claroline forum contains only the category \'Public\', a sample
2482  forum and a sample topic.</p><p>The first thing you should do is delete
2483  the sample topic and modify the first forum\'s name. Then, you can
2484  create, in the \'public\' category, other forums, by groups or by themes, to
2485  fit your learning scenario requirements.</p><p>Don\'t mix Categories and
2486  forums, and don\'t forget that an empty category (without forums) does not
2487  appear in the student view.</p><p>The description of a forum can be the
2488  list of its members, the definition of a goal, a task, a theme...';
2489 $_lang['blockGroupsHelp'] = '<p><b>Introduction</b></p>
2490 <p>This tool allows to create and manage work groups.
2491 At creation (Create groups), groups are emtpy. There are
2492 many ways to fill them:
2493 <ul><li>automatically (\'Fill groups\'),</li>
2494 <li>manually (\'Edit\'),</li>
2495 <li>self-registration by students (Groups settings: \'Self registration allowed...\').</li>
2496 </ul>
2497 These three ways can be combined. You can, for instance, ask students to self-register first.
2498 Then discover that some of them didn\'t and decide then to fill groups automatically in
2499 order to complete them. You can also edit each group to compose membership one student
2500 at a time after or before self-registration and/or automatical filling.</p>
2501 <p>Group filling, whether automatical or manual, works only if there are already students
2502 registered in the course (don\'t mix registration to the course with registration into groups).
2503 Students list is visible in <b>Users</b> tool. </p><hr noshade size=1>
2504 <p><b>Create groups</b></p>
2505 <p>To create new groups, click on \'Create new group(s)\' and determine number of groups to
2506 create. Maximum number of members is optional but we suggest to chose one. If you leave max. field
2507 unchanged, groups size maximum will be infinite.</p><hr noshade size=1>
2508 <p><b>Group settings</b></p>
2509 <p>You can determine Group settings globally (for all groups).
2510 <b>Students are allowed to self-register in groups</b>:
2511 <p>You create empty groups, students self-register.
2512 If you have defined a maximum number, full groups do not accept new members.
2513 This method is good for teachers who do not know the list of students when
2514 creating groups.</p>
2515 <b>Tools</b>:</p>
2516 <p>Every group possesses either a forum (private or public) or a Documents area
2517 (a shared file manager) or (most frequently) both.</p>
2518 <hr noshade size=1>
2519 <p><b>Manual edit</b></p>
2520 <p>Once groups are created (Create groups), you see at bottom of page, a list of groups
2521 with a series of information and functions
2522 <ul><li><b>Edit</b> to modify manually Group name, description, tutor,
2523 members list.</li>
2524 <li><b>Delete</b> deletes a group.</li></ul>
2525 <hr noshade size=1>';
2526 $_lang['blockHomepageHelp'] = 'For convenience, claroline tools contain default entries.
2527  There is a small example in every tool to help you quickly grasp how it
2528  works. It is up to you to modify the example or to delete it.</p><p>For
2529  instance, here on the Home Page of your course website,there is a small
2530  introduction text saying \'This is the introduction text of your course. To
2531  replace it by your own text, click below on modify.\' Click on modify, edit
2532  it and Ok. It\'s that simple. Every tool has the same logic:
2533  add, delete, modify, which is the logic of dynamic websites.</p><p>When
2534  you first create your website, most of the tools are active. Here again,
2535  it is up to you to deactivate the ones you don\'t need. You just have to
2536  click on \'deactivate\'. Then it goes down to the grey section of your
2537  homepage and becomes invisible to your students.  However, you can
2538  reactivate it whenever you want, making it visible to the students once more.</p>
2539 <p>You can add your own pages to your
2540  Home Page. These pages must be HTML pages (which can be created by any
2541  Word Processor or Web Composer). Use \'Upload page and link to Homepage\' to
2542  send your page to the server. The standard header of your website will be
2543  automatically merged with your new document, so that you just need to
2544  concentrate on the content. If you want to link from your Home to
2545  existing websites or pages existing anywhere on the web (even inside your
2546  own site), use \'Add link on Homepage\' The pages you have added to the Home
2547  page can deactivated then deleted, where the standard tools can be
2548  deactivated, but not deleted.</p><p>Once your course website is ready, go
2549  to \'Modify course info\' and decide what level of confidentiality you want.
2550  By default, your course is hidden (because you work on it).</p>';
2551 $_lang['blockIntroCourse'] = 'You are on the course home page.<br /><br />On this page, you can :
2552 <ul>
2553 <li>add portlets to your course home page (see link above);</li>
2554 <li>activate or deactivate tools (click on the \'Edit Tool list\' button at bottom left);</li>
2555 <li>change settings or view statistics (click on corresponding links at bottom).</li>
2556 </ul>';

2581 $_lang['blockUsersHelp'] = '<p>The \'Users\' tool displays user informations in a digest table. Here is below the column descriptions resumed.
2582 <ul>
2583 <li>
2584 <b>Name</b>. By clicking on the username you can see additional informations concerning this user, like e-mail etc.
2585 </li>
2586 <li>
2587 <b>Roles</b>.
2588 Roles have no computer related function. They do not give rights on
2589 operating the system. They just indicate to humans who is who. You can
2590 modify them by clicking on the icon in the \'Edit\' column, then typing whatever
2591 you want: lecturer, assistant, student, visitor, expert...
2592 </li>
2593 <li>
2594 <b>Group tutor</b>. Group tutor is a status allowing a user to coach a group more closely. It gives permission to this user to access all the group area and to see and edit messages on the group forum. You can
2595 modify this status by clicking on the icon in the \'Edit\' column.
2596 </li>
2597 <li>
2598 <b>Course manager</b>. This status is reserved to the people who manage and administrate the course. You can
2599 modify this status by clicking on the icon in the \'Edit\' column.
2600 </li>
2601 <li>
2602 <b>Edit</b> (restricted to course manager). This commands allows course managers to edit user informations related to this course. Course managers are not allowed to modify personal user information like e-mail, name etc, only the data directly related to the course ,like role, tutor status, course manager status, etc. With this command, course managers are also able to create new headings dedicated only this course (see the \'define headings\' button in the user details page). Once headings are defined,each student will be able to fill them.
2603 </li>
2604 <li>
2605 <b>Unregister</b> (restricted to course manager). This command allows course manager to remove a user from their course. It doesn\'t mean the user account don\'t exist anymore, but only that this account is not enrolled to this course.
2606 </li>
2607 </ul>
2608 <h4>
2609 Main commands
2610 </h4>
2611 <ul>
2612 <li>
2613 <b>Add a user</b>. Click on this command to add a user for this course, fill the fields and validate. The person will receive an e-mail telling them they have been registered him/her and telling or reminding them of their login and password.
2614 </li>
2615 <li><b>Add a list of users</b></li> Click on this command to add in a list of several users with a file in CSV format.
2616 </li>
2617 <li>
2618 <b>Subscribe a class</b>. Click on this command to add a collection of users gathered by classes predefined by the platform administrator.
2619 </li>
2620 <li>
2621 <b>Group management</b>. Allows to go directly to the group management tool.
2622 </li>
2623 </ul>
2624 <h4>Tips</h4>
2625 <p>
2626 To allow an assistant, for instance, to co-admin the site, you need to register him in the course or be sure he is already registered, then click on \'modify\' under \'admin rights\', then click \'all\', then \'Ok\'. Co-chairman
2627 </p>
2628 <p>
2629 To mention in the header of the course web site the name of a co-chairman, use the tool \'Modify course information\' (orange tools). This modification does not register your co-chairman as a user of the course. The field \'Lecturers\' is completely independent of the Users list.
2630 Add a user
2631 </p>';
2632 $_lang['blockWarningRemoveInstallDirectory'] = '<b>Notice :</b> The directory containing your Claroline installation process (<code>claroline/install/</code>) is still browsable by the web. It means anyone can reinstall Claroline and crush your previous installation. We highly recommend to protect this directory or to remove it from your server.';
2633 $_lang['blockWikiConflictHowTo'] = '<p><strong>Edit conflict</strong> : The page you try to save seems to have been changed since you modify it.<br /><br />
2634 What to do now ?<ul>
2635 <li>You can copy/paste your modification to a text editor (like notepad) and click on \'edit last version\' to try to add your modification to the new version of the page.</li>
2636 <li>You can also click on cancel to cancel your changes.</li>
2637 </ul></p>';
2638 $_lang['blockWikiHelpAdminContent'] = '<h3>Wiki administration help</h3>
2639 <dl class="wikiHelp">
2640 <dt>How to create a new Wiki ?</dt>
2641 <dd>Click on the link \'Create a new Wiki\'. Then enter the properties of the Wiki :
2642 <ul>
2643 <li><b>Title of the Wiki</b> : choose a title for the Wiki</li>
2644 <li><b>Description of the Wiki</b> : choose a description for the Wiki</li>
2645 <li><b>Access control management</b> : set the access ontrol of the Wiki by checking/uncheking the box (see below)</li>
2646 </ul>
2647 </dd>
2648 <dt>How to enter a Wiki ?</dt>
2649 <dd>Click on the title of the Wiki in the list.</dd>
2650 <dt>How to change the properties of a Wiki ?</dt>
2651 <dd>Click on the icon in the \'Properties\' column in the Wiki list to go to the Wiki properties form.</dd>
2652 <dt>How to use the Access control management options ?</dt>
2653 <dd>You can set the access rights for users by checking/unchecking the box in the \'Access control management\' section of Wiki properties.
2654  You can grant/ungrant access to three types of users :<ul>
2655 <li><b>Course members</b> : users enroll to the course (except the course managers)</li>
2656 <li><b>Group members</b> (only available whithin a group) : users which are members of the group (expect the group\'s tutors)</li>
2657 <li><b>Other users</b> : anonymous users or users which are not course members</li></ul>
2658 For each user type, you can grant three type of privileges to the Wiki(*) :<ul>
2659 <li><b>Read pages</b> : the user of the given type can read the pages of the Wiki</li>
2660 <li><b>Edit pages</b> : the user of the given type can modify the content of th pages of the Wiki</li>
2661 <li><b>Create pages</b> : the user of the given type can create new pages in the Wiki</li>
2662 </ul><small><em>(*) Note that if a user cannot read the pages of a Wiki, he cannot edit or modify them. Note that if a user cannot edit the pages of a Wiki, he cannot create new pages.</em></small></dd>
2663 <dt>How to delete a Wiki ?</dt>
2664 <dd>Click on the icon in the \'Delete\' column to delete a Wiki and all its pages.</dd>
2665 <dt>How to get the list of the pages in a Wiki ?</dt>
2666 <dd>Click on the number of pages of this Wiki in the Wiki list.</dd>
2667 <dt>How to get the list of the last modified pages in a Wiki ?</dt>
2668 <dd>Click on the icon in the \'Recent changes\' column in the Wiki list.</dd>
2669 <dt>How to export a Wiki ?</dt>
2670 <dd>Click on the icon in the \'Export\' column to export a Wiki as a HTML file in the course documents tool.</dd>
2671 </dl>';
2672 $_lang['blockWikiHelpSyntaxContent'] = '<h1>Wiki Syntax</h1>
2673 <h2>Basic syntax</h2>
2674 <dl class="wikiHelp">
2675 <dt>Creating wiki pages and links between them</dt>
2676 <dd><strong>Wiki words</strong> : Wiki words are words written like <em>WikiWord</em>. Wiki2xhtml automaticaly recognise them as Wiki page links. To create a wiki page or to create a link to a wiki page, edit an existing one and add the title of the page in WikiWord syntax, for example <em>MyPage</em>, then save the page. Wiki2xhtml will automaticaly replace the Wiki Word <em>MyPage</em> with a link to the Wiki page <em>MyPage</em>&nbsp;;</dd>
2677 <dd><strong>Wiki links</strong> : Wiki links are like Hyperlinks (see below) expect that they do not contain any protocol scheme (like <em>http://</em> or <em>ftp://</em>) and thatthey are automaticaly recognise as links to Wiki pages. To create a new page or create a link to an existing one using Wiki links, edit a page and add <code>[page title]</code> or <code>[name of link|title of page]</code> to its content. You can also use this syntax to change the text of a WikiWord link : <code>[name of link|WikiWord]</code>.</dd>
2678 <dt>Hyperlinks</dt>
2679 <dd><code>[url]</code>, <code>[name|url]</code>, <code>[name|url|language]</code> or <code>[name|url|language|title]</code>.&nbsp;;</dd>
2680 <dt>Image inclusion</dt>
2681 <dd><code>((url|alternate text))</code>, <code>((url|alternate text|position))</code> ou <code>((url|alternate text|position|long description))</code>. <br />The position argument can take the following values : L (left), R (right) or C (center).&nbsp;;</dd>
2682 <dd>You can use the syntax as Hyperlinks. For example <code>[title|image.gif]</code>. This syntax is deprecated, consider to use the preceding one&nbsp;;</dd>
2683 <dt>Link to an image</dt>
2684 <dd>same as Hyperlinks but put a 1 in fifth argument to avoid image recognition and get an hyperlink to an image. For example <code>[image|image.gif||0]</code> will display a link to image.gif instead of display the imge itself</dd>
2685 <dt>Layout</dt>
2686 <dd><strong>Italic</strong> : surround your text with two single quotes <code>\'\'text\'\'</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2687 <dd><strong>Bold</strong> : surround your text with three single quotes underscores <code>\'\'\'text\'\'\'</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2688 <dd><strong>Underline</strong> : surround your text with two underscores <code>__text__</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2689 <dd><strong>Stroke</strong> : surround your text with two minus symbols <code>--text--</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2690 <dd><strong>Title</strong> : <code>!!!</code>, <code>!!</code>, <code>!</code> respectively for titles, sub-titles and sub-sub-titles&nbsp;;</dd>
2691 <dt>List</dt>
2692 <dd>line starting with <code>*</code> (unordered list) or <code>#</code> (ordered list). You can mix lists (<code>*#*</code>) to create multi-level lists.&nbsp;;</dd>
2693 <dt>Paragraph</dt>
2694 <dd>Separate paragraphs with one or more new lines&nbsp;;</dd>
2695 </dl>
2696 <h2>Advanced syntax</h2>
2697 <dl class="wikiHelp">
2698 <dt>Footnote</dt>
2699 <dd><code>$$footnote text$$</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2700 <dt>Preformated text</dt>
2701 <dd>begin each line of preformated text with a blank space&nbsp;;</dd>
2702 <dt>Cite block</dt>
2703 <dd><code>&gt;</code> or <code>;:</code> before each line&nbsp;;</dd>
2704 <dt>Horizontal line</dt>
2705 <dd><code>----</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2706 <dt>Forced line break</dt>
2707 <dd><code>%%%</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2708 <dt>Acronym</dt>
2709 <dd><code>??acronym??</code> or <code>??acronym|definition??</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2710 <dt>Inline cite</dt>
2711 <dd><code>{{cite}}</code>, <code>{{cite|language}}</code> or <code>{{cite|language|url}}</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2712 <dt>Code</dt>
2713 <dd><code>@@your code here@@</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2714 <dt>Named anchor</dt>
2715 <dd><code>~anchor~</code>&nbsp;;</dd>
2716 </dl>
2717 <h2>Table syntax</h2>
2718 <dl>
2719 <dt>Simple table</dt>
2720 <dd><code>{|</code>&nbsp;: start of table (must be on a new ligne)</dd>
2721 <dd><code>||first cell|second cell|...||</code>&nbsp;: table row (on one line)</dd>
2722 <dd><code>|}</code>&nbsp;: end of table (must be on a new ligne)</dd>
2723 <dt>Complete table</dt>
2724 <dd><code>{|Caption text</code>&nbsp;: start of table (must be on a new ligne)</dd>
2725 <dd><code>||!first column title|!second column title|...||</code>&nbsp;: column header</dd>
2726 <dd><code>||first cell|second cell|...||</code>&nbsp;: table row (on one line)</dd>
2727 <dd><code>|}</code>&nbsp;: end of table (must be on a new ligne)</dd>
2728 </dl>
2729 <h2>Colored text</h2>
2730 <dl>
2731 <dt>Color code (three hexadecimal pairs for red, green and blue)</dt>
2732 <dd><code>//#XXXXXX|text//</code></dd>
2733 <dd>( example :  <code>//#50AF22|Hello//</code>  will produce  <span style="color: #50AF22;">Hello</span> )</dd>
2734 </dl>
2735 <dl>
2736 <dt><a href="couleurs_web.html">Color names</a> ( CSS )</dt>
2737 <dd><code>//color_name|Text//</code></dd>
2738 <dd>( exemple : <code>//red|Hello//</code> will produce <span style="color: red;">Hello</span> )</dd>
2739 </dl>
2740 <em>For Mac OS X users :</em> you can produce the pipe character "|" by pressing Shift+alt+L

2742 <dl>

2746 <dd><code>"""end_html"""</code>&nbsp;: end of raw HTML block</dd>
2747 <dt>Link to MainPage</dt>
2748 <dd><code>"""main"""</code> or <code>"""home"""</code></dd>
2749 <dt>Table of contents</dt>
2750 <dd><code>"""toc"""</code></dd>
2751 </dl>';

  17 abstract class InternalMessage
  18 {
  19     const NOSUBJECT = "No subject";
  20     const NOMESSAGE = "No message";
  21 
  22     protected $sender;
  23     protected $subject;
  24     protected $message;
  25     protected $course = NULL;
  26     protected $group = NULL;
  27     protected $tools = NULL;
  28 
  29     
  30     
  31     
  32     /**
  33      * return the subject of the current message
  34      *
  35      * @return string subject of the message
  36      */
  37     public function getSubject()
  38     {
  39         return $this->subject;
  40     }
  41 
  42     /**
  43      * return the message of the current message
  44      *
  45      * @return string message of the current message
  46      */
  47     public function getMessage()
  48     {
  49         return $this->message;
  50     }
  51 
  52     /**
  53      * return the sender identification
  54      *
  55      * @return int user identification
  56      */
  57     public function getSender()
  58     {
  59         return $this->sender;
  60     }
  61 
  62     /**
  63      * return the course code of the current message (NULL is not existant)
  64      *
  65      * @return string course code
  66      */
  67     public function getCourseCode()
  68     {
  69         return $this->course;
  70     }
  71     
  72     /**
  73      * return the goup identification of the current message (NULL is not existant)
  74      *
  75      * @return int group identification
  76      */
  77     public function getGroupId()
  78     {
  79         return $this->group;
  80     }
  81     
  82     /**

  84      *
  85      * @return string tool identification
  86      */
  87     public function getToolsLabel()
  88     {
  89         return $this->tools;
  90     }    
  91 }

   5 /**
   6  * message to send class
   7  *
   8  * @version     1.9 $Revision: 12923 $
   9  * @copyright   (c) 2001-2011, Universite catholique de Louvain (UCL)
  10  * @author      Claroline Team <info@claroline.net>
  11  * @author      Christophe Mertens <thetotof@gmail.com>

  13  *              GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE version 2 or later
  14  * @package     internal_messaging
  15  */
  16 
  17 
  18 //load internal message class
  19 require_once dirname(__FILE__) . '/internalmessage.lib.php';
  20 // class need to notify bye other way
  21 require_once dirname(__FILE__) . '/../notification/notifier.lib.php';
  22 
  23 class MessageToSend extends InternalMessage
  24 {
  25     
  26     /**
  27      * create an message to send with the information in parameters
  28      *
  29      * @param int $sender user identification
  30      *         if it's not defined it use the current user id
  31      * @param string $subject subject of the message
  32      * @param string $message content of the message
  33      */
  34     public function __construct( $sender = NULL, 
  35         $subject = parent::NOSUBJECT, 
  36         $message = parent::NOMESSAGE )
  37     {
  38         if ( is_null( $sender ) )
  39         {
  40             $sender = claro_get_current_user_id();
  41         }
  42         else
  43         {
  44             $this->sender = $sender;
  45         }
  46         
  47         $this->subject = $subject;
  48         $this->message = $message;
  49     }
  50 
  51     /**
  52      * set the send identification
  53      *
  54      * @param int $senderId sender identification (optional, default NULL)
  55      */
  56     public function setSender($senderId = NULL)
  57     {
  58         if ( is_null( $senderId ) )
  59         {
  60             $sender = claro_get_current_user_id();
  61         }
  62         else
  63         {
  64             $this->sender = $senderId;
  65         }
  66     }
  67 
  68     /**
  69      * set the subject of the current message
  70      *
  71      * @param string $subject suject of the message
  72      */
  73     public function setSubject($subject)
  74     {
  75         $this->subject = $subject;
  76     }
  77 
  78     /**
  79      * set the content of the current message
  80      *
  81      * @param string $message message 
  82      */
  83     public function setMessage($message)
  84     {
  85         $this->message = $message;
  86     }
  87 
  88     /**
  89      * set the course id of the current message
  90      *
  91      * @param string $course course identification
  92      */
  93     public function setCourse($course)
  94     {
  95         $this->course = $course;
  96     }

 171      *   $messageData['subject']

 184     protected function setFromArray($messageData)

 195         }

 201         else
 202         {
 203             throw new Exception("\$messageData['is_deleted'] is not defined: All data must be defined and not null");

 223

 231         }

 243     /**
 244      * create a new ReceviedMessage with the information in the parameter
 245      *
 246      * @param array $messageData
 247      *   $messageData['message_id']
 248      *   $messageData['subject']
 249      *   $messageData['message']
 250      *   $messageData['sender']
 251      *   $messageData['send_time']
 252      *   $messageData['course']
 253      *   $messageData['group']
 254      *   $messageData['tools']
 255      *   $messageData['is_read']
 256      *   $messageData['is_deleted']
 257      *   $messageData['user_id']
 258      *   $messageData['firstName']
 259      *   $messageData['lastName']
 260      * 
 261      * @return ReceivedMessage the message created
 262      */
 263     public static function fromArray($messageData)
 264     {
 265         $message = new ReceivedMessage($messageData['message_id']);
 266         
 267         $message->setFromArray($messageData);       
 268          
 269         return $message;
 270     }
 271 
 272     /**
 273      * create a new message
 274      *
 275      * @param int $messageId message identification
 276      * @param int $userId user identification
 277      * if it not defined it use the current user identification
 278      * @return ReceivedMessage the message created
 279      */
 280     public static function fromId($messageId, $userId = NULL)
 281     {
 282         if ( is_null( $userId ) )
 283         {
 284             $userId = claro_get_current_user_id();
 285         }
 286         
 287         if ( ! claro_is_platform_admin() )
 288         {
 289             $userSql = " AND R.user_id = " . (int) $userId ."\n";
 290         }
 291         else
 292         {
 293             $userSql = "";
 294         }
 295          
 296         $tableName = get_module_main_tbl(array('im_message','im_message_status','user','im_recipient'));
 297          
 298         $messageSQL =
 299             "SELECT U.nom AS lastName, U.prenom AS firstName, M.message_id, M.sender,M.subject,  \n"
 300                 ."M.message, M.send_time, R.is_read, R.is_deleted, R.user_id, M.course, M.group, M.tools, \n"
 301                 ."RE.sent_to\n"
 302                 .    "FROM `" . $tableName['im_message'] . "` as M \n"
 303                 .    " LEFT JOIN `".$tableName['im_message_status']."` AS R ON M.message_id = R.message_id\n"
 304                 .    " LEFT JOIN `".$tableName['user']."` AS U ON M.sender = U.user_id\n"
 305                 ." LEFT JOIN `".$tableName['im_recipient']."` AS RE ON M.message_id = RE.message_id\n"
 306                 .    " WHERE M.message_id = " . (int) $messageId."\n"
 307                 . $userSql
 308                 ;
 309 
 310         $resultMessage = claro_sql_query_fetch_single_row($messageSQL);
 311         
 312         if (!$resultMessage)
 313         {
 314             $messageSQL =
 315                 "SELECT U.nom AS lastName, U.prenom AS firstName, M.message_id, M.sender, M.subject, \n"
 316                 ."M.message, M.send_time, R.is_read, R.is_deleted, R.user_id, M.course, M.group, M.tools, \n"
 317                 ."RE.sent_to\n"
 318                 ."FROM `" . $tableName['im_message'] . "` as M\n"
 319                 ." LEFT JOIN `".$tableName['im_message_status']."` AS R ON M.message_id = R.message_id\n"
 320                 ." LEFT JOIN `".$tableName['user']."` AS U ON M.sender = U.user_id\n"
 321                 ." LEFT JOIN `".$tableName['im_recipient']."` AS RE ON M.message_id = RE.message_id\n"
 322                 ." WHERE R.user_id = 0" 
 323                 ." AND M.message_id = " . (int) $messageId
 324                 ;
 325             $resultMessage = claro_sql_query_fetch_single_row($messageSQL);
 326         }
 327         if(!$resultMessage)
 328         {
 329             return false;
 330         }
 331         else
 332         {
 333             return self::fromArray($resultMessage);
 334         }
 335     }
 336 
 337     /**
 338      * load the current message from the data base
 339      */
 340     public function load()
 341     {
 342         $tableName = get_module_main_tbl(array('im_message','im_message_status','user','im_recipient'));
 343         
 344         $messageSQL =
 345             "SELECT U.nom AS lastName, U.prenom AS firstName, M.message_id, M.sender, M.subject, \n"
 346             ."M.message, M.send_time, R.is_read, R.is_deleted, R.user_id , M.course, M.group, M.tools, \n"
 347             ."RE.sent_to"
 348             ." FROM `" . $tableName['im_message'] . "` as M \n"
 349             ." LEFT JOIN `".$tableName['im_message_status'] . "` as R ON M.message_id = R.message_id\n"
 350             ." LEFT JOIN `".$tableName['user']."` AS U ON M.sender = U.user_id\n"
 351             ." LEFT JOIN `".$tableName['im_recipient']."` AS RE ON M.message_id = RE.message_id\n"
 352             ." WHERE R.user_id = " . (int) $this->userId."\n"
 353             ." AND M.message_id = " . (int) $this->messageId."\n"
 354             ;
 355         
 356         $this->setFromArray(claro_sql_query_fetch_single_row($messageSQL));
 357     }
 358 
 359     public function isPlatformMessage()
 360     {
 361         return $this->sentTo == 'allUser';
 362     }
 363 }

   4 
   5 /**
   6  * message box  class (abstract)
   7  *
   8  * @version     1.9 $Revision: 13687 $
   9  * @copyright   (c) 2001-2011, Universite catholique de Louvain (UCL)
  10  * @author      Claroline Team <info@claroline.net>

  13  *              GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE version 2 or later
  14  * @package     internal_messaging
  15  */
  16 
  17 abstract class MessageBox implements CountableIterator
  18 {
  19     protected $messageFilter = NULL;
  20     protected $messageList = FALSE;
  21     protected $numberOfMessage = FALSE;
  22     protected $index;
  23     protected $userId;
  24 
  25     /**
  26      * create an object MessageBox for the user in parameters and with strategy
  27      *
  28      * @param MessageStrategy $strategy strategy to apply
  29      * @param int $userId user identification of the message box (optionnal, default: current_user_id())
  30      *     
  31      */
  32     public function __construct($strategy, $userId = NULL)
  33     {
  34         if (is_null($userId))
  35         {
  36             $userId = claro_get_current_user_id();
  37         }
  38         
  39         $this->messageFilter = $strategy;
  40         $this->index = 0;
  41         $this->userId = $userId;
  42     }
  43 
  44     /**
  45      * add 1 to the index for the iterator
  46      *
  47      */
  48     public function next()
  49     {
  50         // If message list not loaded, load it !
  51         $this->loadMessageList();
  52         
  53         $this->index += 1;
  54     }
  55 
  56     /**
  57      * check if the message in index $index exist
  58      *
  59      * @return boolean
  60      */
  61     public function valid()
  62     {
  63         // If message list not loaded, load it !
  64         $this->loadMessageList();
  65         
  66         if ($this->index > count($this->messageList)-1)
  67         {
  68             return false;
  69         }
  70         else
  71         {
  72             return true;
  73         }
  74     }
  75 
  76     /**
  77      * Load the list of message
  78      *
  79      */
  80     abstract public function loadMessageList();
  81     
  82     /**
  83      * return the number of message in the messageBox
  84      * 
  85      * @return int number of message
  86      */
  87     abstract public function getNumberOfMessage();
  88     
  89     /**
  90      *
  91      * @return int the identification of the current message
  92      */
  93     public function key()
  94     {
  95         return $this->messageList[$this->index]['message_id'];
  96     }
  97 
  98     /**
  99      * return the message strategy
 100      *
 101      * @return MessageStrategy
 102      */
 103     public function getMessageStrategy()
 104     {
 105         return $this->messageFilter;
 106     }
 107     
 108     /**
 109      * set the message filter
 110      *
 111      * @param MessageFilter $messageFilter filter
 112      */
 113     public function setMessageStrategy($messageFilter)
 114     {
 115         $this->messageFilter = $messageFilter;
 116     }
 117     
 118     /**
 119      * return the iterator to begin
 120      *
 121      */
 122     public function rewind()
 123     {
 124         $this->index = 0;
 125     }
 126

  16 
  17 
  18 //load messagebox class
